- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at 1.5–2x recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag by 1–3 days in reaction to sentiment shifts; apply 1–2 day lead-in adjustment if sentiment changes sharply.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.10), model often underperforms; add 0.2–0.5 point upward bias to avoid underestimation.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 prices are rising, don’t assume continuation; add 0.3–0.7 point downward buffer if sentiment is weak.
